root_cause: Syntax._get_syntax computed code_width from options.max_width (minus the line-number column) without subtracting the horizontal padding. With word_wrap=True the code was wrapped to the full console width, and __rich_console__ then wrapped the result in Padding, so each wrapped line overflowed the console by pad_left+pad_right cells and was re-wrapped (issue #3727: padding plus word wrap). Gold also stores padding unpacked via a PaddingProperty descriptor so self.padding is always a 4-tuple, and changes `if self.padding:` to `if any(self.padding)`.
best_solution: In rich/syntax.py Syntax._get_syntax, unpack the padding (`_, right, _, left = Padding.unpack(self.padding)`), subtract left+right from the auto-computed code_width in both the line_numbers and plain branches (only when code_width is None), and clamp code_width at 0. That alone is enough for the hidden test; the gold descriptor and `any(self.padding)` change are refactors that the test does not need.
acceptable_alternatives: Any change that makes the auto code_width equal max_width - numbers_column - pad_left - pad_right when code_width is None. v7's patch (subtract horizontal padding inside the conditional, clamp at 0) passes the full rich suite locally under Pygments 2.20.0 / Python 3.12 (853 passed, same as gold).
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_syntax.py::test_padding_plus_wrap: Console(width=24, file=StringIO(), legacy_windows=False), Syntax("'Hello, World. This should wrap.'", lexer='python', padding=(0, 3), word_wrap=True); console.print(syntax) must write exactly "   'Hello, World.       \n   This should wrap.'   \n". The rest of the test patch only adds `-> None` annotations and moves an import.
locating_signals: Title 'Syntax padding' names the class (rich/syntax.py Syntax) and the attribute (padding). The issue text (unavailable to the agent) adds word_wrap. Grep for `padding` in syntax.py finds __rich_measure__ (which already unpacks padding) and _get_syntax (which does not): the asymmetry between measure and render is the signal.
our_outcome_summary: Kaggle env: all four configs scored FAIL. v4 (163 s, 51 calls) committed only a repo-root test_syntax_padding.py about padding background colour, with no source change. v6 (64 s, 24 calls) and v8 (195 s, 39 calls) produced empty patches. v7 (84 s, 20 calls, 1110 chars) made the correct fix in _get_syntax (subtract horizontal padding from code_width, clamp at 0). The Kaggle rescore (eval/kaggle/rescore_fair) marks v7 resolved=False with exit 1, but a local rerun on the rich_3782 snapshot with Pygments 2.20.0 (the Kaggle kernel's pin) and Python 3.12 gives 25/25 in tests/test_syntax.py and 853 passed in the full suite, identical to gold. Under Pygments 2.21 both gold and v7 fail the same 7 snapshot tests. So the v7 FAIL label is contradicted by the local rerun and needs a Kaggle-env recheck with test output captured.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is 'X padding' / 'X margin' plus an issue link, look for two code paths that compute the same width: the measure path and the render path. If one subtracts the padding and the other does not, make the render path match. Content wrapped inside a Padding or border must be wrapped to max_width minus the horizontal padding, not the full width. And never submit only a test file: a bugfix title always needs a source change.
